fields.description:
Mirror inventory finding F11 (`reports/stability/mirror-inventory.md`), LOW.

## Problem

- `src/rebar/_cli/_registry.py` `ROUTES` — the live route names
- `src/rebar/_cli/_execute.py:22` `_CROSS_SESSION_WARN_COMMANDS` — 14 hardcoded SPELLINGS, used at `:74`

All 14 are live route names today, so this is preventive. A route RENAME silently drops the
warning: `:74` is `if name not in _CROSS_SESSION_WARN_COMMANDS`, so a stale spelling simply never
matches and the cross-session warning disappears with nothing failing.

## Scope — what is and is not the mirror (epic AC2)

WHICH verbs warn cross-session is a DISTINCT CONCEPT: a policy subset, the same shape that makes
`_NOT_CLAIMABLE_STATUSES` not a mirror. This ticket does not touch that judgement and must not
change which commands warn.

The mirror is ONLY the SPELLINGS, which must be route names and are not enforced to be. This is
the one CLI policy subset not folded into `derive_policy_sets` (`_registry.py:680`), where every
other such subset already lives.

## Approach — add-route-flag

Give `Route` a `warn_cross_session` flag, set it on those 14 routes, and fold the set into
`derive_policy_sets` beside its siblings. The spellings then ARE route names by construction, and a
rename carries the flag automatically.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC1: the warn set is derived from `ROUTES` via `derive_policy_sets`; `_execute.py` no longer
      carries a spelling list. Verified by a test asserting the derived set is used and the literal
      is gone.
- [ ] AC2: the membership is UNCHANGED — exactly the same 14 commands warn. Verified by a test
      pinning the derived set against the 14 names the literal carried, so the refactor cannot
      quietly change policy.
- [ ] AC3: every warn-flagged name is a live route name. Verified by a test asserting the derived
      set is a subset of live `ROUTES` names, which is the property a hardcoded list could violate.
- [ ] AC4: renaming a route carries its warning. Verified by a test that renames a flagged route in
      a synthetic registry and asserts the derived set follows the new name.

## Testing

- `python -m pytest tests/unit -k "registry or execute or cross_session or policy" -q` — AC1-AC4.
- `make lint && make typecheck`.
